theConflict.whatTheDispatchAsks: P-362 requirement 3: 'The script resolves `gcloud` on Windows (and on Linux still), with the fix stated' - reading, with the preceding sentence, as a change to scripts/check-tagged-revision-env.mjs.
theConflict.whyThatIsNotWhatWasDone: That file's bytes are LOAD-BEARING AND PINNED. pr-checks.yml's `p279-tagged-revision-env-divergence` job requires it to be byte-identical to hauska-engine's tools/check-tagged-revision-env.mjs and REFUSES on any difference; its own header says so and its canonical record names the engine path. So an edit to this file in this repo alone turns that gate RED until a coupled engine PR lands with the same bytes. The dispatch's own scope line is 'You build in legacy-design-tools only and open one PR', and the file's header warns that the two copies must not drift. The two instructions cannot both be satisfied in one PR, so this lane did not silently pick one.
theConflict.whatWasDoneInstead: The resolution was put in the wrapper, which is LDT-only and unpinned: it decides the gcloud NAME and hands it to the check through P279_GCLOUD. `gcloud.cmd` on win32, `gcloud` elsewhere; a configured P279_GCLOUD the check's SHELL_SAFE guard would refuse is discarded and named on stderr with the substitute. This was OBSERVED WORKING ON THE LIVE SERVICE (see liveWindows below), which is what the requirement's own verification asks for.
theConflict.whatThatDoesNotFix: The check's own `gcloudBinary()` still returns `process.env.P279_GCLOUD || "gcloud"` with no win32 branch, so any caller that invokes check-tagged-revision-env.mjs DIRECTLY with a spaced P279_GCLOUD still gets SERVICE_DESCRIBE_FAILED. Named as an OPEN item, not claimed as closed.
theConflict.theRulingRequested: Either (a) accept the wrapper-level resolution as satisfying requirement 3 for the entry point this row documents, and that is already the shipped state; or (b) rule that the check itself must carry the win32 branch, in which case this row needs a SECOND PR against hauska-engine with byte-identical content and the LDT PR re-pinned to it - the two MUST merge in an order that never leaves the divergence gate red across a night. The exact patch for (b) is three lines in `gcloudBinary()` (a win32 branch returning `gcloud.cmd`) plus the same bytes in the engine copy, and it is deliberately NOT written here because writing it without the coupled PR is the drift the gate exists to catch.

theThreeQuestionGate.q: What executes the check after a shift?
theThreeQuestionGate.a: The `shift-traffic` job of the workflow for that service (cloud-run-deploy.yml for cortex-api, cloud-run-deploy-smartsite-mcp.yml for smartsite-mcp), as its last step, named `Tagged-revision credential check (P-279) [after traffic shift]`. It runs `node scripts/p279-tagged-revision-check.mjs --project <GCP_PROJECT_ID> --region us-central1 --service <CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE>`, which spawns `scripts/check-tagged-revision-env.mjs --json <same flags>` and reads its report. The same wrapper also runs from `deploy-canary` in both workflows as the first check.

A `workflow_dispatch` with `inputs.action = shift-traffic` (the job's own `if:`). Nothing on `push` reaches it: the deploy workflows' traffic jobs are unreachable from a push event by construction, which is this repo's stated hard constraint.

theThreeQuestionGate.q: What fails when a tag points at a revision missing a credential?
theThreeQuestionGate.a: The predicate returns FAIL for that service; the wrapper prints `p279-tagged-revision-env: RESULT=violation - a tag points at a revision missing a credential the serving revision carries`, names the tag, the revision and the missing names, and exits 1. The step fails under GitHub's default `bash -e`, so the job fails. Nothing is mutated: removing or repointing a tag is an operator decision and the check says so in its own output.

theThreeQuestionGate.q: Is that failure distinguishable from the check not running?
theThreeQuestionGate.a: Yes, and it is the whole point of the change. `did-not-run` is a different word, a different exit code (2 vs 1), different text (`RESULT=did-not-run` plus the child's exit code and the last lines of its stderr) and it is produced by the absence of a service verdict rather than by a verdict. The 2026-09-18 run is the measured proof that this was NOT true before: a missing module produced the string `RESULT=violation - a tag points at a revision missing a credential the serving revision carries` on a clean service.

(1) A hand `gcloud run deploy --tag` or `gcloud run services update-traffic` outside the workflow - no step runs at all, and a tag can be created or repointed with nothing watching. (2) A shift performed by the `rollback` action, which changes traffic to a named revision and has no P-279 step: it can leave the pre-existing tag set pointing at whatever it pointed at, unexamined. (3) A workflow that calls check-tagged-revision-env.mjs directly instead of the wrapper - pr-checks.yml does this for its two OFFLINE jobs, which is fine (no service to read), but a future live call site that copies that pattern would reintroduce the numeric mapping. (4) A `run:` step that discards the exit code, or a `continue-on-error: true` added to the step. (5) Editing or deleting the wrapper in the same PR that changes a tag policy - it is a repo file, so whoever can change the workflow can change the check. All five are named in the wrapper's own header under WHAT BYPASSES IT, because the answer is never 'nothing'.

liveWindows.host: win32, node v24.11.1, `where gcloud` resolves to C:\Users\cente\AppData\Local\Google\Cloud SDK\google-cloud-sdk\bin\gcloud
liveWindows.theCauseReproduced: Raw check with P279_GCLOUD set to the real spaced install path returned `verdict: REFUSE`, `reason: SERVICE_DESCRIBE_FAILED`, `detail: unsafe argument refused (shell metacharacter or quote): "C:\\Users\\cente\\AppData\\Local\\Google\\Cloud SDK\\google-cloud-sdk\\bin\\gcloud.cmd"`. That is the check's OWN guard refusing the binary's path, not a shell-quoting accident in execFileSync - the distinction the dispatch asked to capture rather than guess.
liveWindows.theFixObserved: The wrapper in the SAME environment returned `RESULT=clean`, exit 0, with stderr naming both the discarded value and the substitute: `P279_GCLOUD="C:\\...\\Google Cloud SDK\\..." contains a space or a quote and the check refuses such an argument; using gcloud.cmd from PATH instead`.
liveWindows.liveVerdictToday: cortex-api's tags read CLEAN at 2026-09-18T18:25Z from this lane, which is consistent with the hand check recorded in the incident record and is the value an operator should see on the next shift.
liveWindows.conditionDependence: With P279_GCLOUD UNSET the raw check also passed on this host - cmd.exe resolves `gcloud` through PATHEXT and the guard never sees a space. So the dispatch's 'on a Windows host the script refuses' is condition-dependent: it requires an operator to have pointed P279_GCLOUD at the real path, which is the natural thing to do and which produces the failure. A fix that only changed the default would have missed the seat's case.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.q: A6 - the shim `gcloud.cmd` is pinned by NAME. What if a Windows runner has gcloud installed somewhere not on PATH?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.disposition: Then the check REFUSES with a describe failure and the wrapper reads `did-not-run`, which is the safe direction. But it is a real limit: this fix improves the operator case on a Windows host where the SDK is on PATH, which is the case the seat hit. The alternative (accepting a spaced path and quoting it correctly inside the check) is the (b) branch of theConflict.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.q: A7 - does the wrapper make the step depend on one new file that could itself be missing?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.disposition: Yes - and a missing wrapper reads `did-not-run` only if Node gets far enough to run it, which it cannot. If the wrapper is absent the step fails with Node's own `Cannot find module` and exit 1, and no RESULT line is printed at all. That is not a false violation (nothing claims one), but it is a bare failure, and it is why the checkout is half the fix and both halves are in this PR.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.q: A8 - is `clean` returned by the wrapper ever produced without a PASS verdict from the predicate?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.disposition: No. `clean` requires every result to have a string `service` and `verdict`, at least one result, no FAIL anywhere, no REFUSE anywhere, exactly one distinct verdict and that verdict PASS. Falsifier F9 shows an unrecognised-but-verdict-shaped report does NOT produce clean. The residual: the wrapper trusts the child's JSON as the report, so a child that printed a fabricated PASS would be believed - that is the check's own integrity problem and is what pr-checks.yml's canonical divergence compare covers.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.q: A9 - could this change make a real violation harder to see?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.disposition: Only by adding the word did-not-run to the vocabulary, and only for failures to run, which previously produced the word violation - so a real violation is now the ONLY thing that produces `violation`. The step still fails in every non-clean case.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.q: A10 - the wrapper's own docstring says an earlier draft mis-handled the fixture shape. Why record a self-inflicted bug in the shipped file?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDelivera.disposition: Because the next person to tighten that marker needs to know a too-tight marker was already tried and what it did. It is one sentence and it is the difference between a comment and a record.
